references.text: God gave Moses the two stone tablets, written with God's finger, as a direct parallel to Deuteronomy 9:10.
Describes the two tablets that were written on both sides, a testimony written with God's finger.
God commands Moses to carve out two new stone tablets like the first ones, referring to the original tablets mentioned in Deuteronomy 9:10.
Describes the people gathering at the mountain when God spoke from the fire, which is the 'day of assembly' mentioned in Deuteronomy 9:10.
The Lord gives Moses stone tablets with the law and commandments that God has written.
The Lord proclaimed His covenant, the Ten Commandments, and wrote them on two stone tablets.
The Lord spoke these words to the entire assembly at the mountain from the fire, and wrote them on two stone tablets.
Retelling of how God wrote the Ten Commandments on the tablets, the same words He spoke from the fire on the day of assembly.
Paul contrasts stone tablets with tablets of the heart, referring to the living Spirit of God instead of God's finger.
